title: Python for IT
subtitle: Guess the hidden Python terms -- spin for consonants, buy vowels

puzzles.hint: This arithmetic operation rounds a quotient down to the nearest whole number, discarding any remainder.
puzzles.explain: The `//` operator performs integer division: `7 // 2` evaluates to `3`, not `3.5`. Unlike regular `/`, it always returns a whole number (or a float with a zero decimal if one operand is a float).

puzzles.hint: A technique for extracting a portion of text using a start index and a stop index separated by a colon.
puzzles.explain: Writing `s[1:4]` extracts characters at positions 1, 2, and 3 -- the stop index is excluded. Negative indices count from the end, so `s[-3:]` grabs the last three characters.

puzzles.hint: A compact, one-line construct that builds a new sequence from an existing iterable, optionally applying a filter condition.
puzzles.explain: `[x * 2 for x in range(4)]` produces `[0, 2, 4, 6]` in a single expression. An optional `if` clause lets you skip elements, making it far more concise than an equivalent `for` loop with `.append()`.

puzzles.hint: A control structure that intercepts runtime problems and lets a program respond gracefully instead of crashing.
puzzles.explain: A `try` block wraps risky code, and an `except` block specifies what to do if a particular error occurs. An optional `finally` block runs regardless of whether an error was raised, making it ideal for cleanup.

puzzles.hint: The keyword that passes a computed value back to the caller when a function finishes executing.
puzzles.explain: When Python reaches `return value`, it immediately exits the function and hands `value` back to the code that called it. A function with no explicit `return` automatically hands back `None`.

puzzles.hint: A mechanism that allows one class to acquire the behavior and data of another, reducing repeated code.
puzzles.explain: A child class listed with a parent in parentheses -- `class Dog(Animal):` -- gains all of the parent's methods and attributes automatically. The child can override any inherited method to provide specialized behavior.

puzzles.hint: A specific built-in exception raised when bracket notation is used to look up an entry that does not exist in a mapping.
puzzles.explain: Accessing `d['missing']` on a dictionary that has no such entry triggers this exception immediately. Using `d.get('missing')` is the safe alternative -- it returns `None` (or a default you specify) instead of raising.

puzzles.hint: An isolated workspace that keeps a project's third-party packages separate from the system-wide interpreter.
puzzles.explain: Running `python -m venv venv` creates a self-contained directory holding its own Python interpreter and a private `site-packages` folder. Activating it ensures that `pip install` affects only that project, preventing version conflicts across projects.
